headline: Strong storm brings wind, rain, and coastal flooding through Thursday; brief weekend break.
summary: A strong storm system is moving in from the Pacific tonight, with a front bringing widespread rain and wind to western Washington through Thursday. A weaker system follows Friday, then a weak area of high pressure aloft brings a brief break this weekend, with mostly dry weather expected. The active pattern returns next week, though forecasters are less sure of the details. For most people, that means a wet, windy night and Thursday. The strongest gusts, up to around 60 mph, are likely on the outer coast, with strong winds in the Puget Sound lowlands too. Coastal flooding is the main concern as high tides, storm surge, and big waves combine, mostly around Thursday morning. The northern Cascades could see significant snow.
changes: Later updates raised the expected peak gusts on the outer coast to around 60 mph, from 50 to 55 mph earlier. Models also came to agree well on the weekend break, which forecasters had described as less certain in the morning.
